checkpoints.description: [1/2] while-true back edge emits a bare jmp instead of movabs/test/jne; [2/2] read_char prologue loads cursor and count with mov_load_rip instead of lea_rip+mov_load

impact_assessment.why: char_stream pays ~14 instructions per byte: the caller back edge lowers the literal-true loop condition to movabs+test+jne (10 wasted bytes + 2 uops per byte), and read_char's prologue loads cursor/count via lea_rip+mov_load pairs (20 bytes) where direct rip loads are 12
impact_assessment.benefits: every while-true loop in every cairn program drops 2 dead uops on its back edge; read_char's hot fall-through prologue shrinks by 8 instructions-bytes, measurable on the 4M-iteration char_stream scoreboard case
impact_assessment.risks: contract: emitted code shape changes for while-true loops only - same semantics because the condition is the literal true; dependency: new consumer for the existing mov_load_rip helper only, no new machine helpers; concurrency: none - static single-threaded image; state: cursor/count slot layout unchanged, only their load encoding
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first shape tests for both lowering changes; same-window stash A/B on char_stream with output-identity check; full gate --save --compare plus quiet-window re-run rule; fast revert if A/B shows any regression

checkpoints.description: [1/3] cairn/optimize.py: pure-function inlining (single-return callees, slot-preserving substitution, multi-use-argument hoisting with slot bumps, recursion and size guards); [2/3] algebraic pass: distributive expansion of constant coefficients over add-chains plus like-term collection (wrapping ring algebra, call-free signature groups); [3/3] pipeline order, full suite, failing-first tests, benchmark --save --compare, ADR-067

impact_assessment.why: user goal is faster than C/C++/Rust; gcc wins many_params by inlining and folding 31i+37(i+1)+... to 216i+252 while cairn pays six materialized arguments and a call per iteration; the gap is structural, not per-benchmark
impact_assessment.benefits: benefits: inlining removes call overhead for the general class of pure single-return functions; distributive expansion plus like-term collection folds linear argument algebra; both apply to any program, no benchmark special cases
impact_assessment.risks: contract: passes reorder nothing observable but multi-use hoisting can permute which of two trapping arguments traps first (same exit 3, same stdout; stderr message order only). dependency: optimizer mutates sema-assigned slots; fresh hoist slots must bump function.slots or the frame misaligns. concurrency: no shared state. state: emitted bytes change, so the benchmark gate returns
impact_assessment.mitigation: contract: evaluation order preserved by substituting in left-to-right arg order and hoisting before the statement; trapping-only divergence documented in ADR. dependency: fresh slots numbered from the caller's existing slots count, zip-pinned by tests. state: full unittest gate plus python -m benchmarks.run_benchmarks --save --compare before phase 4
